items.q: A 3-day-old male neonate develops poor feeding, progressive lethargy, and vomiting. Blood gas reveals respiratory alkalosis with an ammonia level of 680 mcmol/L. Urine organic acid profiling demonstrates massively elevated orotic acid with undetectable citrulline. Which is the deficient enzyme?
items.exp: Ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency is the most common urea cycle disorder (X-linked recessive). Deficient OTC causes mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate accumulation, which spills into the cytosol and enters pyrimidine synthesis via CPS-II, resulting in massive urinary orotic acid alongside severe hyperammonemia.
r: Incorrect. CPS-I deficiency presents with hyperammonemia but LOW or absent urinary orotic acid.
Correct. OTC deficiency produces severe hyperammonemia coupled with massively elevated urinary orotic acid.
Incorrect. Argininosuccinate lyase deficiency causes elevated argininosuccinic acid.
Incorrect. UMP synthase deficiency causes orotic aciduria with NORMAL ammonia and megaloblastic anemia.

items.q: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (CPS-I) in the mitochondrial matrix requires which obligate allosteric activator for catalytic activity?
items.exp: CPS-I requires N-acetylglutamate as an obligate allosteric activator. N-acetylglutamate is synthesized by NAG synthase from acetyl-CoA and glutamate, which is allosterically stimulated by arginine after a protein-rich meal.
r: Correct. N-acetylglutamate is the obligate allosteric activator of CPS-I.
Incorrect. Argininosuccinate is a downstream intermediate.
Incorrect. Citrulline is formed by ornithine transcarbamylase.
Incorrect. Carbamoyl phosphate is the product.

items.q: A male infant presents on day 3 of life with hyperammonemia, lethargy, respiratory alkalosis, and markedly elevated urinary orotic acid. Which X-linked enzyme is deficient?
items.exp: OTC deficiency is the most common urea cycle disorder and the only one that is X-linked recessive. Carbamoyl phosphate accumulates and leaks into the cytosol, driving pyrimidine synthesis and massive urinary orotic acid excretion.
r: Correct. OTC deficiency is X-linked and causes hyperammonemia with elevated urinary orotic acid.
Incorrect. CPS-I deficiency causes hyperammonemia with low or absent orotic acid.
Incorrect. Argininosuccinate synthetase is autosomal recessive (citrullinemia).
Incorrect. NAGS deficiency causes low orotic acid.

items.q: In the urea cycle, which amino acid enters the pathway by providing the second nitrogen atom incorporated into the final urea molecule?
items.exp: One nitrogen of urea derives from free ammonium ion via CPS-I; the second nitrogen atom is supplied by aspartate when it condenses with citrulline via argininosuccinate synthetase.
r: Correct. Aspartate donates the second nitrogen of urea in the cytosol.
Incorrect. Glutamate provides ammonium via glutamate dehydrogenase, contributing the first nitrogen.
Incorrect. Alanine transports nitrogen from muscle to liver.
Incorrect. Glutamine carries nitrogen from peripheral tissues.

items.q: Which reaction of the urea cycle generates fumarate, providing an essential metabolic bridge (the 'Krebs bicycle') linking the urea cycle to the citric acid cycle?
o: Cleavage of argininosuccinate by argininosuccinate lyase
Synthesis of argininosuccinate by argininosuccinate synthetase
items.exp: Argininosuccinate lyase cleaves argininosuccinate into arginine and fumarate. Fumarate is converted to malate and enters the citric acid cycle or gluconeogenesis, linking the two cycles.
r: Correct. Argininosuccinate lyase releases fumarate, connecting to the TCA cycle.
Incorrect. Argininosuccinate synthetase condenses citrulline and aspartate.
Incorrect. Arginase cleaves arginine to urea and ornithine.
Incorrect. OTC generates citrulline.

items.q: What pharmacological agent is administered in urea cycle disorders to scavenge nitrogen by conjugating with glycine to form hippuric acid, which is rapidly excreted in urine?
items.exp: Sodium benzoate conjugates with glycine to form hippurate (hippuric acid), which is rapidly cleared by renal glomerular filtration and secretion, removing one nitrogen atom per molecule.
r: Correct. Sodium benzoate conjugates with glycine to form hippurate.
Incorrect. Sodium phenylbutyrate conjugates with glutamine to form phenylacetylglutamine.

items.q: Which two reactions of the urea cycle take place inside the mitochondrial matrix before the remaining steps occur in the cytosol?
items.exp: The first two reactions (synthesis of carbamoyl phosphate by CPS-I and synthesis of citrulline by OTC) occur inside the mitochondrial matrix. Citrulline is then transported to the cytosol for the remaining three reactions.

Incorrect. Argininosuccinate synthetase and lyase are cytosolic.

o: De novo synthesis of arginine within the urea cycle is abolished
